title: Eddie Durham, Glenn Miller and "Slip Horn Jive" at the Famous Door
summary: Jones says Eddie Durham took Basie arrangements to Glenn Miller's band, and Miller stopped visiting the Famous Door after Basie played "Slip Horn Jive" without music.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: That's right... He left to go to build Glenn Miller's band. J: He took "Slip Horn Jive" that was a trombone solo that nobody played but Benny Morton and myself, and he made his first big record. He was at the Glen Island Casino.
With what band?
Glenn Miller.
Durham played with Glenn Miller?
He took it out of Basie's book and gave it to Glenn Miller.
JONES 98
What I'm trying to find out from you, did Ed Durham just arrange for him or did Durham play in the band?
He arranged for the band.
This is what I wondered because I don't remember - do you remember any black people in Glenn Miller's band?
Of course not.
This is what I'm trying to get at, and Ed Durham is black.
Ed Durham is black, the first one to put the guitar -
This is what I'm trying to find. Did Ed Durham play -
No, he didn't play. He was an arranger, like Sy Oliver eventually came with. He didn't play.
This is where Freddie Green came in, right? He was already there? I see.
This had no interference with that because Durham could still play the trombone and double on guitar on certain special things that never was recorded, not in the band, you see.
What year was this when Ed Durham went with Glenn Miller?
Just a little before we came out of Auburn, New York. He left us -
Was this '38 or '39?
JONES 99

About the first of '38 he left us to go to be an arranger and Glenn Miller was forming his band. Eddie Durham which we recorded with on the thing down on Christopher Street, took arrangements from the Basie band to build Mr. Glenn Miller's band. Now Glenn was-
Where was he playing, at the Glen Island Casino?
That's right, 'cause we opened the Famous Door July 1938. We stayed there 5 1/2 weeks - I mean 5 1/2 months.
Where was the Famous Door - that was on 52nd Street?

52nd Street. When Mr. Glenn Miller had made 'Slip Horn Jive' that Martin Block and everybody was playing on the radio, he came in and when we played 'Slip Horn Jive' without the music, Mr. Glenn Miller did not come back in the Famous Door anymore. He used to come there every night from the Glen Isle Casino, but when we played 'Slip Horn Jive' with no music, he left. He never came around Count Basie's band any more in life.
